title: Stripe provider - build vs community crate (decision record)

overview.problemStatement: BP-014 is a decision before it is code: Stripe is absent from the provider catalogue, so developers either build their own client or pick a community crate with unknown maintenance, licence, and MSRV fit, and wirekit 0.2.x scope cannot be fixed without the answer.
overview.proposedSolution: A decision record that scores building a stripe module against documenting a community crate on six fixed criteria, with crates.io evidence and dates, a recommendation, and explicit revisit triggers. Gate 1 chose Option B: document async-stripe 0.41.0 (MIT OR Apache-2.0, rust-version 1.82.0, published 2025-04-08). No code, dependency, or catalogue file is added.
overview.targetAudience: The maintainer deciding wirekit 0.2.x scope, and Rust developers who need payments.
assumptions: wirekit has no Stripe code today (no stripe module under crates/wirekit/src).
CON-104 requires providers to ship as wirekit modules; CON-105 requires a catalogue design file first.
Evidence comes from the crates.io API on 2026-10-31; no further external review was performed (CON-704).
outOfScope: Any Stripe implementation, dependency, or catalogue design file.
Billing domain logic such as invoices, subscription lifecycles, and tax (CON-106).

userStories.title: Decide with evidence
userStories.want: both options scored against fixed criteria
userStories.benefit: 0.2.x scope is a recorded decision rather than an assumption

acceptanceCriteria.text: Given the decision record, when it is read, then both options are scored against C1..C6 with crates.io evidence and dates.
Given Gate 1 approval, when the record is finalised, then it names the chosen option and the approver, with no option left implied.
Given the build option is chosen, when the record is finalised, then it states that CON-105 requires a catalogue design file and enumerates the exact surface.
Given the community-crate option is chosen, when the record is finalised, then it pins crate name, version, licence, MSRV, and the documentation pointer.
Given the record, when the decision later needs revisiting, then the triggers are explicit: async-stripe 1.0 stable, an MSRV change, a Stripe API break, or the crate becoming unmaintained.

functionalRequirements.text: The record MUST evaluate both options against the six criteria with cited evidence.
The record MUST name the chosen option and its rationale after Gate 1 approval.
If the build option is chosen, the record MUST require a catalogue design file under CON-105 and enumerate the exact surface.
If a community crate is chosen, the record MUST pin name, version, licence, MSRV, and the documentation pointer.
The record MUST define revisit triggers for the decision.

nonFunctionalRequirements.text: Evidence MUST carry source and date; unknown facts MUST stay marked [to be confirmed] (CON-704).
A chosen community crate MUST be licence-compatible and MUST NOT raise the workspace MSRV without a constitution amendment (CON-102, CON-111).
This record MUST NOT add code, dependencies, or a catalogue file; it is a decision only (CON-103).

edgeCases.description: async-stripe publishes a stable release whose MSRV exceeds 1.85
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The fallback (Option A) becomes the recommendation.
Option A with the narrow surface is the only viable path.

edgeCases.description: Stripe ships a breaking API change that neither option covers
edgeCases.expectedBehavior: The revisit trigger fires and the record is reopened.

risks.description: The recommendation rested on an unverified MSRV for async-stripe 0.41.x.
risks.mitigation: Closed at Gate 1: 0.41.0 declares rust-version 1.82.0, so it fits the 1.85 workspace MSRV.

risks.description: A decision record can decay into a stale opinion.
